greek: Ἐκάλεσεν δὲ Ιακωβ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπεν Συνάχθητε, ἵνα ἀναγγείλω ὑμῖν, τί ἀπαντήσει ὑμῖν ἐπʼ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν·
hint: Jacob calls his sons together to tell them what will meet them in the last days.

notes.text: Upon the last of the days, for the Hebrew bĕʾaḥărît hayyāmîm, the latter end of the days.
Aorist passive imperative of συνάγω: be gathered together.

reading: [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[name:Ιακωβ]] the sons of him and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[be brought together|be brought together, be gathered together, be collected, be convened, be joined in one and united, be received into a house, be drawn together and narrowed and contracted, be concluded and inferred|συνάγω]], [[that|that, in order that|ἵνα]] [[I may carry back tidings of|I may carry back tidings of, I may report|ἀναγγέλλω]] to you, what [[will move from|will move from, will meet, will meet and encounter, will come|ἀπαντάω]] to you [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of outermost|of outermost, of furthest and uttermost and extreme, of last, of uppermost, of lowest and deepest, of innermost|ἔσχατος]] [[of the days|of the days, of the day-breaks, of the times|ἡμέρα]];

names.gloss: (Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")

greek: ἀθροίσθητε καὶ ἀκούσατε, υἱοὶ Ιακωβ, ἀκούσατε Ισραηλ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν.
hint: He bids the sons of Jacob gather and listen to Israel their father.

notes.text: ἀκούω with the genitive of the one heard: listen to Israel.

reading: [[be gathered together|be gathered together and mustered, be gathered, be collected, collect yourselves|ἀθροίζω]] and [[hear|hear, have hearing of, hear tell of, know by hearsay, hearken and give ear, listen to and obey|ἀκούω]], sons of [[name:Ιακωβ]], [[hear|hear, have hearing of, hear tell of, know by hearsay, hearken and give ear, listen to and obey|ἀκούω]] of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather|πατήρ]] of you.

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")

greek: Ρουβην, πρωτότοκός μου σύ, ἰσχύς μου καὶ ἀρχὴ τέκνων μου, σκληρὸς φέρεσθαι καὶ σκληρὸς αὐθάδης.
hint: Jacob names Reuben his firstborn and his strength, but hard and self-willed.

notes.text: Hard to bear and hard, self-willed. The Hebrew has yeter śĕʾēt wĕyeter ʿāz, pre-eminent in dignity and pre-eminent in power.
The beginning of my children: ἀρχή, first cause and first place, for the Hebrew rēʾšît ʾônî, the first of my strength.

names.gloss: (Ρουβην, from Hebrew Rĕʾûbēn, which the Hebrew of 29:32 hears in rāʾâ bĕʿonyî, "he has seen my affliction")

greek: ἐξύβρισας ὡς ὕδωρ, μὴ ἐκζέσῃς· ἀνέβης γὰρ ἐπὶ τὴν κοίτην τοῦ πατρός σου· τότε ἐμίανας τὴν στρωμνήν, οὗ ἀνέβης.
hint: Jacob likens Reuben's insolence to water and recalls that he went up to his father's bed.

notes.text: You broke out in insolence like water; do not boil over. The Hebrew has paḥaz kammayim ʾal-tôtar, unstable as water, you shall not excel.
Where you went up: the second person still. The Hebrew turns to the third, ʿālâ, he went up.
μή with the aorist subjunctive, a prohibition: do not boil over.

reading: [[you broke out into insolence|you broke out into insolence and ran riot and waxed wanton|ἐξυβρίζω]] [[as|as, according as, considering, like|ὡς]] [[water|water, waters, rain-water and rain, water of a water-clock|ὕδωρ]], [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[you may boil out|you may boil out or over, you may break out|ἐκζέω]]; [[you went up|you went up, you mounted, you ascended, you went up to, you rose, you came up, you came to and arrived at, you went up country, you went aboard|ἀναβαίνω]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[the marriage-bed|the marriage-bed, the lair, the nest, the act of going to bed, the bed, the chambering and lasciviousness|κοίτη]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather|πατήρ]] of you; [[at that time|at that time, then, in those times and formerly, at one time|τότε]] [[you stained|you stained, you dyed, you defiled and sullied, you tainted and defiled|μιαίνω]] [[the bed spread|the bed spread or prepared, the bed and couch, the mattress and bedding|στρωμνή]], where [[you went up|you went up, you mounted, you ascended, you went up to, you rose, you came up, you came to and arrived at, you went up country, you went aboard|ἀναβαίνω]].

greek: Συμεων καὶ Λευι ἀδελφοί· συνετέλεσαν ἀδικίαν ἐξ αἱρέσεως αὐτῶν.
hint: Jacob calls Simeon and Levi brothers who did wrong by their own choice.

notes.text: They accomplished wrong out of their choice. The Hebrew has kĕlê ḥāmās mĕkērōtêhem, weapons of violence their swords, or their plans.
First a taking, then a choosing, a deliberate plan, and later a sect: the word heresy comes from it.

reading: [[name:Συμεων]] and [[name:Λευι]] [[sons of the same mother|sons of the same mother, brothers, near kinsmen|ἀδελφός]]; [[brought quite to an end|brought quite to an end and completed and accomplished, made up the whole and the number, paid towards common expenses and contributed, belonged to a class and were counted in it|συντελέω]] [[wrong-doing|wrong-doing and injustice, wrong and injury|ἀδικία]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of a taking|of a taking, of means for taking a place, of a taking for oneself and a choosing and choice, of election, of a choice and deliberate plan and purpose, of a sect and school, of a religious sect, of a heresy|αἵρεσις]] of them.

names.gloss: (Συμεων, from Hebrew Šimʿôn, which the Hebrew of 29:33 hears in šāmaʿ, "he heard")
(Λευι, from Hebrew Lēwî, which the Hebrew of 29:34 hears in lāwâ, "he was joined")

greek: εἰς βουλὴν αὐτῶν μὴ ἔλθοι ἡ ψυχή μου, καὶ ἐπὶ τῇ συστάσει αὐτῶν μὴ ἐρείσαι τὰ ἥπατά μου, ὅτι ἐν τῷ θυμῷ αὐτῶν ἀπέκτειναν ἀνθρώπους καὶ ἐν τῇ ἐπιθυμίᾳ αὐτῶν ἐνευροκόπησαν ταῦρον.
hint: Jacob wants no part in their counsel, recalling the men they killed in anger and the bull they hamstrung.

notes.text: My livers. The Hebrew has kĕbōdî, my glory, which the Greek reads as kĕbēdî, my liver, from the same consonants.
Two aorist optatives with μή, wishes against: may my soul not come, may my livers not lean.
ἐρείδω, to make lean, to prop, to press hard: Middle Liddell lacks it, and LSJ's active senses stand here.

reading: [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[will|will and determination, a counsel and piece of advice and plan and design, a council of the elders or chiefs and a senate|βουλή]] of them [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[may it come|may it come, may it go, may it go back and return, may it be going to and intend, may it come within a little of and be near|ἔρχομαι]] [[the breath|the breath, the life, the spirit, life and death, the ghost, the departed soul|ψυχή]] of me, and [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + dative]] [[to the putting together|to the putting together and composition, to the studied expression, to the bringing together and introduction and recommendation, to the standing together and meeting, to the close combat and conflict, to the conflict, to the meeting and knot of men, to the political union, to the friendship or alliance, to the conspiracy, to the construction and structure and constitution, to the political constitution, to the contraction and sternness and sullenness|σύστασις]] of them [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[may it cause to lean|may it cause to lean and prop, may it fix firmly and plant, may it prop up and support and stay, may it press hard and attack, may it push and thrust, may it infix and plant in, may it inflict, may it press down and depress, may it match and set against, may it settle upon, may it exert pressure, may it rest, may it set to work and fall to, may it become fixed|ἐρείδω]] the livers of me, [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[in the soul|within, inside of, and by means of the soul, the spirit and heart, the anger and wrath, the mind and temper, the will and desire, the courage and spirit|ἐν; ἐπιθυμία]] of them [[hamstrung|hamstrung and houghed|νευροκοπέω]] a bull.

greek: ἐπικατάρατος ὁ θυμὸς αὐτῶν, ὅτι αὐθάδης, καὶ ἡ μῆνις αὐτῶν, ὅτι ἐσκληρύνθη· διαμεριῶ αὐτοὺς ἐν Ιακωβ καὶ διασπερῶ αὐτοὺς ἐν Ισραηλ.
hint: Jacob curses their stubborn anger and says he will divide and scatter them in Israel.

notes.text: Middle Liddell's only gloss is yet more accursed, ἐπί strengthening κατάρατος.
σκληρύνω, to harden, in the passive: it was hardened.

reading: yet more accursed [[the soul|the soul, the spirit and heart, the anger and wrath, the mind and temper, the will and desire, the courage and spirit|θυμός]] of them, [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[self-willed|self-willed and wilful and dogged and stubborn and contumacious and presumptuous, remorseless and unfeeling|αὐθάδης]], and [[the wrath|the wrath and anger|μῆνις]] of them, [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] was hardened; [[I will distribute|I will distribute, I will divide|διαμερίζω]] them [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to [[name:Ιακωβ]] and [[I will scatter abroad|I will scatter abroad, I will throw about, I will squander|διασπείρω]] them [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to [[name:Ισραηλ]].

greek: Ιουδα, σὲ αἰνέσαισαν οἱ ἀδελφοί σου· αἱ χεῖρές σου ἐπὶ νώτου τῶν ἐχθρῶν σου· προσκυνήσουσίν σοι οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ πατρός σου.
hint: Jacob wishes Judah his brothers' praise and his enemies' defeat, with his father's sons bowing to him.

notes.text: May they praise you: an aorist optative, a wish. The Hebrew has the imperfect yôdûkā, they shall praise you, playing on yĕhûdâ, Judah; the Greek loses the play.
The vocative of Ιουδας: Judah, addressed.

names.gloss: (Ιουδας, from Hebrew Yĕhûdâ, which the Hebrew of 29:35 hears in yādâ, "to praise")

greek: σκύμνος λέοντος Ιουδα· ἐκ βλαστοῦ, υἱέ μου, ἀνέβης· ἀναπεσὼν ἐκοιμήθης ὡς λέων καὶ ὡς σκύμνος· τίς ἐγερεῖ αὐτόν;
hint: Jacob pictures Judah as a lion's whelp that lies down where none will rouse it.

notes.text: From a shoot. The Hebrew has miṭṭerep̄, from the prey; ṭerep̄ is also a fresh leaf, and the Greek reads that.
You lay down, still in the second person. The Hebrew turns to the third, kāraʿ rābaṣ, he crouched, he lay down.

reading: [[a cub|a cub and whelp, a lion's whelp|σκύμνος]] [[of a lion|of a lion, of a lion's skin|λέων]] [[name:Ιουδα]]; [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] [[of sprout|of sprout and shoot and sucker|βλαστός]], son of me, [[you went up|you went up, you mounted, you ascended, you went up to, you rose, you came up, you came to and arrived at, you went up country, you went aboard|ἀναβαίνω]]; [[having fallen back|having fallen back, having fallen back and given ground, having flagged and lost heart, having been given up, having reclined|ἀναπίπτω]] [[you were lulled|you were lulled, you were hushed to sleep and put to sleep, you were lulled to rest and stilled and calmed, you fell asleep, you went abed and lay abed, you slept, you fell asleep and died, you kept watch at night|κοιμάω]] [[as|as, according as, considering, like|ὡς]] [[a lion|a lion, a lion's skin|λέων]] and [[as|as, according as, considering, like|ὡς]] [[a cub|a cub and whelp, a lion's whelp|σκύμνος]]; who [[will awaken|will awaken and wake up and rouse, will rouse and stir up, will stir, will raise, will raise and erect|ἐγείρω]] him?

greek: οὐκ ἐκλείψει ἄρχων ἐξ Ιουδα καὶ ἡγούμενος ἐκ τῶν μηρῶν αὐτοῦ, ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ τὰ ἀποκείμενα αὐτῷ, καὶ αὐτὸς προσδοκία ἐθνῶν.
hint: Jacob foresees rule staying with Judah until what is laid up for him comes, and the nations waiting on him.

notes.lemma: ἕως ἂν ἔλθῃ τὰ ἀποκείμενα αὐτῷ
notes.text: Until the things laid up for him come. The Hebrew has ʿad kî-yābōʾ šîlōh, until Shiloh comes, which the Greek reads as šellô, what is his.
A ruler and one leading, persons, for the Hebrew šēbeṭ and mĕḥōqēq, a sceptre and a ruler's staff; and from his thighs, where the Hebrew has from between his feet.
The expectation of nations. The Hebrew has yiqqĕhat ʿammîm, the obedience of peoples.

greek: δεσμεύων πρὸς ἄμπελον τὸν πῶλον αὐτοῦ καὶ τῇ ἕλικι τὸν πῶλον τῆς ὄνου αὐτοῦ· πλυνεῖ ἐν οἴνῳ τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν αἵματι σταφυλῆς τὴν περιβολὴν αὐτοῦ·
hint: Jacob pictures Judah tethering his colt to the vine and washing his robe in wine.

notes.text: ἕλιξ, anything that coils, a vine's tendril, for the Hebrew śōrēqâ, the choice vine. Middle Liddell's second entry, the noun; the first is the adjective, twisted.
Future: he will wash. The Hebrew has the perfect kibbēs.

greek: χαροποὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ οἴνου, καὶ λευκοὶ οἱ ὀδόντες αὐτοῦ ἢ γάλα.
hint: Jacob pictures Judah's eyes bright with wine and his teeth white as milk.

notes.text: Glad-eyed from wine. The Hebrew has ḥaklîlî ʿênayim miyyāyin, darker of eyes than wine; the Greek takes min as from, not than.
White … than milk: ἤ, than, after a positive adjective, as the Hebrew min after lĕbon.
Middle Liddell prints a tooth inside its Latin, Lat. dens, dentis, a tooth; MARKUP_LOST restores it, and with one sense the word is plain text.

greek: Ζαβουλων παράλιος κατοικήσει, καὶ αὐτὸς παρʼ ὅρμον πλοίων, καὶ παρατενεῖ ἕως Σιδῶνος.
hint: Jacob places Zebulun by the sea, at an anchorage of ships, reaching toward Sidon.

notes.text: Beside an anchorage of ships: ὅρμος is first a cord or chain, then a roadstead, a haven.
Future of παρατείνω, to stretch out along, here of a territory reaching.

names.gloss: (Ζαβουλων, from Hebrew Zĕbûlûn, which the Hebrew of 30:20 hears in zābal, "to dwell with honour")
(Σιδών, from Hebrew Ṣîdōn, usually connected with ṣûd, "to hunt, to fish")

greek: Ισσαχαρ τὸ καλὸν ἐπεθύμησεν ἀναπαυόμενος ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν κλήρων·
hint: Jacob says Issachar set his heart on the good, resting among the allotments.

notes.text: Desired the good. The Hebrew has ḥămōr gārem, a bony donkey; the Greek reads ḥmr as from ḥāmad, to desire.
Between the lots. The Hebrew has bên hammišpĕtāyim, between the sheepfolds or the saddle-bags.

reading: [[name:Ισσαχαρ]] [[the beautiful|the beautiful, the beauteous, the fair, the good|καλός]] [[set his heart upon|set his heart upon, lusted after and longed for and coveted and desired|ἐπιθυμέω]] [[desisting from|desisting from, taking his rest and sleeping, halting and resting, regaining strength|ἀναπαύω]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] [[of the lots|of the lots, of the casting lots and drawing lots, of the allotments, of the pieces of land and portions and farms, of the clergy|κλῆρος]];

names.gloss: (Ισσαχαρ, from Hebrew Yiśśāśkār, which the Hebrew of 30:18 hears in śākār, "wages")

greek: καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν ἀνάπαυσιν ὅτι καλή, καὶ τὴν γῆν ὅτι πίων, ὑπέθηκεν τὸν ὦμον αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ πονεῖν καὶ ἐγενήθη ἀνὴρ γεωργός.
hint: Jacob says Issachar, finding rest good and the land rich, bent his shoulder to toil and became a farmer.

notes.text: He became a man, a tiller of the ground. The Hebrew has wayhî lĕmas-ʿōbēd, and became a slave at forced labour.
The articular infinitive after εἰς: for the toiling.
πίων serves for the feminine here, with γῆ, as Middle Liddell's ὁ, ἡ allows.

greek: Δαν κρινεῖ τὸν ἑαυτοῦ λαὸν ὡσεὶ καὶ μία φυλὴ ἐν Ισραηλ.
hint: Jacob says Dan will judge his own people as one tribe in Israel.

notes.text: κρίνω is first to separate, then to judge. The Hebrew yādîn, he shall judge, plays on Dān; the Greek loses the play.
His own people: the reflexive between the article and its noun, read here after the noun.

reading: [[name:Δαν]] [[will separate|will separate and part and put asunder and distinguish, will pick out and choose, will pick out for himself and choose, will decide, will judge, will adjudge, will judge of and estimate, will expound and interpret, will determine, will question, will bring to trial and accuse, will pass sentence upon and condemn|κρίνω]] [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]] of himself [[just as if|just as if and as though, about|ὡσεί]] [[also|also and even, but, nay, and yet, as, likewise|καί]] [[one|one, a single one and one alone|εἷς]] [[race|race, tribe, body united by ties of blood and descent, clan, tribe by local habitation, hundred and county, contingent furnished by a tribe, brigade|φυλή]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to [[name:Ισραηλ]].

names.gloss: (Δαν, from Hebrew Dān, which the Hebrew of 30:6 hears in dîn, "he judged")

greek: καὶ γενηθήτω Δαν ὄφις ἐφʼ ὁδοῦ ἐγκαθήμενος ἐπὶ τρίβου, δάκνων πτέρναν ἵππου, καὶ πεσεῖται ὁ ἱππεὺς εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω.
hint: Jacob wishes Dan to be a snake by the road that bites the horse's heel and throws its rider.

notes.text: Let Dan become: an imperative, a wish. The Hebrew has yĕhî, let him be, and šĕp̄îp̄ōn, a horned viper, where the Greek has ὄφις ἐγκαθήμενος, a serpent lying in wait.
The article over the adverb: into the things behind, backwards.

reading: and [[let come into being|let come to be, let arise, let be brought into existence|γίνομαι]] [[name:Δαν]] [[serpent|serpent and snake|ὄφις]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of way|of way, of path, of track, of road, of highway, of course, of journey, of manner and method|ὁδός]] [[sitting in or on|sitting in or on, lying in ambush|ἐγκάθημαι]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of a worn or beaten track|of a worn or beaten track and the high road and highway, of a footpath, of rubbing and attrition, of delay|τρίβος]], [[biting|biting, champing, stinging or pricking|δάκνω]] [[heel|heel, the under part of the heel, the ham|πτέρνα]] [[of horse|of horse and mare, of horse and cavalry|ἵππος]], and [[will fall|will fall, will fall down, will fall violently upon and attack, will throw himself down and fall down, will fall and be ruined, will fall and sink, will fall short and fail, will fall and turn out, will be lucky, will fall under and belong to|πίπτω]] [[the horseman|the horseman, the charioteer, the hero who fights from a chariot, the rider, the horsemen or knights, the king's body guard|ἱππεύς]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] the things [[backwards|backwards, back and back again, again, hereafter, behind, following|ὀπίσω]].

greek: τὴν σωτηρίαν περιμένω κυρίου.
hint: Jacob breaks off to say he waits for the Lord's salvation.

notes.text: I wait for the salvation of the Lord, κυρίου a genitive. The Hebrew addresses him, lîšûʿātĕkā qiwwîtî yhwh, for your salvation I wait, O LORD.

reading: [[the saving|the saving and deliverance and preservation and safety, the safe return, the keeping safe, the security and guarantee for safety|σωτηρία]] [[I wait for|I wait for and await, I await and am in store for, I wait and stand still|περιμένω]] [[of lord|of lord / master, of the head, of master, of the Lord, of Jehovah|κύριος]].

greek: Γαδ, πειρατήριον πειρατεύσει αὐτόν, αὐτὸς δὲ πειρατεύσει αὐτῶν κατὰ πόδας.
hint: Jacob plays on Gad's name: a raiding band will raid him, and he will raid at their heels.

notes.text: The Greek keeps the Hebrew's play, gĕdûd yĕgûdennû … yāgud, a raiding band raiding, with one root three times. Middle Liddell's πειρατήριον is first an ordeal, then a pirates' nest.
πειρατεύω, to be a pirate, one translation: plain text.

reading: [[name:Γαδ]], [[ordeal|ordeal, a pirate's nest|πειρατήριον]] will be a pirate him, he [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], will be a pirate of them [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[feet|feet, talons, feet of a hill|πούς]].

names.gloss: (Γαδ, from Hebrew Gād, which the Hebrew of 30:11 hears in gād, "fortune")

greek: Ασηρ, πίων αὐτοῦ ὁ ἄρτος, καὶ αὐτὸς δώσει τρυφὴν ἄρχουσιν.
hint: Jacob says Asher's bread will be rich and he will supply delicacies to rulers.

notes.text: Luxury for rulers. The Hebrew has maʿădannê-melek, a king's dainties.

reading: [[name:Ασηρ]], [[fat|fat and plump, fat and rich, rich and wealthy, plenteous|πίων]] of him [[the cake|the cake, the loaf of wheat-bread, the bread|ἄρτος]], and he [[will give|will give, will grant, will provide, will give over and deliver up|δίδωμι]] [[softness|softness and delicacy and daintiness, luxuries, luxuriousness and wantonness|τρυφή]] [[to rulers|to rulers and commanders and chiefs and captains, to chief magistrates|ἄρχων]].

names.gloss: (Ασηρ, from Hebrew ʾĀšēr, which the Hebrew of 30:13 hears in ʾōšer, "happiness")

greek: Νεφθαλι στέλεχος ἀνειμένον, ἐπιδιδοὺς ἐν τῷ γενήματι κάλλος.
hint: Jacob likens Naphtali to a stock growing freely and yielding beauty in its fruit.

notes.text: A stock let loose. The Hebrew has ʾayyālâ šĕluḥâ, a hind let loose; the Greek reads ʾêlâ, a terebinth, from the same consonants.
Giving beauty in its produce. The Hebrew has hannōtēn ʾimrê-šāp̄er, who gives words of beauty.
The perfect passive participle of ἀνίημι, to send up, let go: let loose, and so standing.

reading: [[name:Νεφθαλι]] [[crown of the root|crown of the root and stump|στέλεχος]] [[having been sent up|having been sent up and forth and standing so, having been made to spring up, having been produced, having been sent back and put back and opened, having been let go and left, having been let go unpunished, having been let loose at, having been set on and urged, having been let go for, having been set free from, having been let and allowed, having been let go free and left untilled, having been slackened and relaxed and let down and unstrung, having been remitted and neglected and given up, having devoted oneself and given oneself up, having slackened and abated, having given way, having given up and ceased, having ceased from|ἀνίημι]], [[giving besides|giving besides, giving in dowry, giving freely, contributing as a benevolence, increasing and advancing, growing and waxing and advancing and improving|ἐπιδίδωμι]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to the produce [[beauty|beauty, pleasure, a beauty, rich garments and stuffs, beautiful works|κάλλος]].

names.gloss: (Νεφθαλι, from Hebrew Naptālî, which the Hebrew of 30:8 hears in niptal, "I have wrestled")

greek: Υἱὸς ηὐξημένος Ιωσηφ, υἱὸς ηὐξημένος ζηλωτός, υἱός μου νεώτατος· πρός με ἀνάστρεψον.
hint: Jacob calls Joseph a son grown great and envied, his youngest, and bids him turn back to him.

notes.text: A son increased, for the Hebrew bēn pōrāt, a fruitful bough, read from pārâ, to be fruitful.
Envied, my youngest son, turn back to me. The Hebrew has ʿălê-ʿāyin bānôt ṣāʿădâ ʿălê-šûr, by a spring, its branches run over the wall; the Greek reads the line otherwise throughout.

reading: son [[having been made large|having been made large and increased and augmented and standing so, having been increased in power and strengthened and exalted and aggrandised, having been promoted to honour and glorified and magnified, having grown and waxed and increased, having grown up|αὐξάνω]] [[name:Ιωσηφ]], son [[having been made large|having been made large and increased and augmented and standing so, having been increased in power and strengthened and exalted and aggrandised, having been promoted to honour and glorified and magnified, having grown and waxed and increased, having grown up|αὐξάνω]] [[to be emulated|to be emulated and worthy of imitation, to be deemed happy and to be envied, enviable and blessed|ζηλωτός]], son of me [[youngest|youngest, most youthful, newest and freshest, strangest|νέος]]; [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] me [[turn upside down|turn upside down, upset, turn back and bring back, rally, turn back and return and retire, dwell, conduct yourself, revolve, face about|ἀναστρέφω]].

names.gloss: (Ιωσηφ, from Hebrew Yôsēp̄, which the Hebrew of 30:24 hears in yōsēp̄, "may he add")

greek: εἰς ὃν διαβουλευόμενοι ἐλοιδόρουν, καὶ ἐνεῖχον αὐτῷ κύριοι τοξευμάτων·
hint: Jacob recalls the plotters who reviled Joseph and the archers who pressed him hard.

notes.text: Lords of arrows: the Hebrew baʿălê ḥiṣṣîm, archers, word for word.
Two imperfects: they kept reviling, they kept pressing.

reading: [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] whom [[discussing pro and con|discussing pro and con and discussing thoroughly|διαβουλεύομαι]] [[were abusing|were abusing and reviling, were rebuking|λοιδορέω]], and [[were holding within|were holding within, were laying up and cherishing inward, were entering in and piercing, were pressing upon and being urgent against|ἐνέχω]] to him [[lords|lords / masters, the heads, masters|κύριος]] [[of things which are shot|of things which are shot and arrows, of bowshots, of archery|τόξευμα]];

greek: καὶ συνετρίβη μετὰ κράτους τὰ τόξα αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐξελύθη τὰ νεῦρα βραχιόνων χειρῶν αὐτῶν διὰ χεῖρα δυνάστου Ιακωβ, ἐκεῖθεν ὁ κατισχύσας Ισραηλ·
hint: Jacob says their bows were broken by the hand of Jacob's mighty one, the one who strengthened Israel.

notes.text: Their bows were broken. The Hebrew has wattēšeb bĕʾêtān qaštô, his bow stayed firm: the Greek makes it the enemies' bows.
The sinews were loosed. The Hebrew has wayyāpōzzû zĕrōʿê yādāyw, his arms were made agile.
Thence he who strengthened Israel. The Hebrew has miššām rōʿeh ʾeben yiśrāʾēl, thence the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel.
A singular verb with the neuter plural τόξα, as Greek has it.

reading: and [[was rubbed together|was rubbed together, was shivered to atoms, was beaten to a jelly and crushed|συντρίβω]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] [[of strength|of strength and might, of might and power, of rule and sway and sovereignty, of power over, of a power and an authority, of mastery and victory|κράτος]] [[the bows|the bows, the bows and arrows, the rays|τόξον]] of them, and [[was loosed|was loosed and released and set free, was unloosed and unstrung, was relaxed and enfeebled, was brought to an end|ἐκλύω]] [[the sinews|the sinews and tendons, the tendons of the feet, the sinews and vigour, the guts and cords made of sinew, the cords of a sling|νεῦρον]] of arms [[of hands|of hands, of hands and arms, of arms|χείρ]] of them [[through|through, throughout and over, during, by aid of and by means of, by reason of, because of, for the sake of|διά + accusative]] [[hand|hand, hand and arm, arm|χείρ]] [[of a lord|of a lord and master and ruler|δυνάστης]] of [[name:Ιακωβ]], [[from that place|from that place and thence, thereafter and next|ἐκεῖθεν]] [[the one having had power over|the one having had power over and overpowered and prevailed against, the one having come to his full strength|κατισχύω]] [[name:Ισραηλ]];

greek: παρὰ θεοῦ τοῦ πατρός σου, καὶ ἐβοήθησέν σοι ὁ θεὸς ὁ ἐμὸς καὶ εὐλόγησέν σε εὐλογίαν οὐρανοῦ ἄνωθεν καὶ εὐλογίαν γῆς ἐχούσης πάντα· ἕνεκεν εὐλογίας μαστῶν καὶ μήτρας,
hint: Jacob calls down on Joseph his father's God's help and blessings of heaven, earth, breast and womb.

notes.text: My God. The Hebrew has wĕʾēt šadday, and by Shaddai.
A blessing of the earth that holds all things. The Hebrew has birkōt tĕhôm rōbeṣet tāḥat, blessings of the deep that crouches beneath.
Aorists: he helped, he blessed. The Hebrew has the imperfects, he will help, he will bless.

reading: [[from the side of|from the side of, from beside, from, near|παρά + genitive]] [[of God|of everything that God is by nature, of deity in full and undiminished kind|θεός]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather|πατήρ]] of you, and [[came to aid|came to aid and succoured and assisted and aided, gave aid and came to the rescue|βοηθέω]] to you [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[the mine|the mine, the to me and relating to me and against me, the by me|ἐμός]] and [[spoke well of|spoke well of, praised, honoured, blessed|εὐλογέω]] you [[good language|good language, fine language, a fair speech and specious talk, eulogy and panegyric, blessing|εὐλογία]] [[of heaven|of heaven, of vault, of firmament and sky|οὐρανός]] [[from above|from above and on high, from the upper country, above and on high, from the beginning, by descent, over again and anew|ἄνωθεν]] and [[good language|good language, fine language, a fair speech and specious talk, eulogy and panegyric, blessing|εὐλογία]] [[of earth|of earth, of land, of ground|γῆ]] [[of having|of having, of holding, of possessing, of keeping, of dwelling in and inhabiting, of holding fast, of bearing up against and supporting|ἔχω]] [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]]; [[on account of|on account of, for the sake of, because of, for, as far as regards|ἕνεκα]] [[of good language|of good language, of fine language, of a fair speech and specious talk, of eulogy and panegyric, of blessing|εὐλογία]] [[of ones of the breasts|of ones of the breasts, of women's breasts, of udders, of round hills and knolls, of pieces of wool|μαστός]] and of womb,

greek: εὐλογίας πατρός σου καὶ μητρός σου· ὑπερίσχυσεν ἐπʼ εὐλογίαις ὀρέων μονίμων καὶ ἐπʼ εὐλογίαις θινῶν ἀενάων· ἔσονται ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν Ιωσηφ καὶ ἐπὶ κορυφῆς ὧν ἡγήσατο ἀδελφῶν.
hint: Jacob says his blessings outweigh those of the lasting mountains and will rest on Joseph's head.

notes.text: Of abiding mountains. The Hebrew has hôray, my parents, which the Greek reads as hărărê, mountains, as the parallel line suggests.
Of the brothers whom he led. The Hebrew has nĕzîr ʾeḥāyw, the one set apart from his brothers.
Of everlasting heaps: θίς, a heap, a sand-bank, for the Hebrew gibʿōt ʿôlām, the everlasting hills.

reading: [[of good language|of good language, of fine language, of a fair speech and specious talk, of eulogy and panegyric, of blessing|εὐλογία]] [[of father|of father, of grandfather|πατήρ]] of you and [[of mother|of mother, of dam, of source|μήτηρ]] of you; [[was exceedingly strong|was exceedingly strong, was too luxuriant, was overbearing, was stronger than and prevailed over|ὑπερισχύω]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + dative]] [[to good languages|to good languages, to fine languages, to fair speeches and specious talks, to eulogies and panegyrics, to blessings|εὐλογία]] [[of mountains|of mountains and hills|ὄρος]] [[of staying in one's place|of staying in one's place and stable and steadfast, of abiding and lasting and stable|μόνιμος]] and [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + dative]] [[to good languages|to good languages, to fine languages, to fair speeches and specious talks, to eulogies and panegyrics, to blessings|εὐλογία]] [[of heaps|of heaps, of sand-heaps and sand-banks, of beaches and shores, of sand, of mud, of very bottoms|θίς]] [[of ever-flowing|of ever-flowing, of everlasting|ἀέναος]]; will be [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[head|head, the life, the top, the brim, the coping, the source, the crown and completion|κεφαλή]] of [[name:Ιωσηφ]] and [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of head|of head and top and highest point, of crown, of top or peak, of sum and substance, of height, of choicest and noblest and best|κορυφή]] of whom [[went before|went before and led the way, led the way for, guided and conducted, was leader in, led, led and conducted, was the leader or commander of, supposed and believed and held, held or regarded, believed in, thought fit and deemed necessary|ἡγέομαι]] [[of sons of the same mother|of sons of the same mother, of brothers, of near kinsmen|ἀδελφός]].

greek: Βενιαμιν λύκος ἅρπαξ· τὸ πρωινὸν ἔδεται ἔτι καὶ εἰς τὸ ἑσπέρας διαδώσει τροφήν.
hint: Jacob likens Benjamin to a ravening wolf that eats in the morning and shares out food at evening.

notes.text: Will eat still. The Hebrew has yōʾkal ʿad, will devour prey; the Greek reads ʿad, prey, as ʿôd, still.
Will distribute food. The Hebrew has yĕḥallēq šālāl, will divide spoil.
πρωινός, the later form of πρώιος, early; the neuter with the article, in the morning.

reading: [[name:Βενιαμιν]] a wolf [[rapacious|rapacious, rapine, a robber and plunderer|ἅρπαξ]]; [[the early|the early, the early in the day and at early morn, the early in the year|πρωινός]] [[will eat|will eat, will eat of|ἐσθίω]] [[yet|yet, as yet, still, further, besides, moreover|ἔτι]] and [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] the thing [[of evening|of evening, of eventide, of eve, of nightfall, of the west|ἑσπέρα]] [[will give from hand to hand|will give from hand to hand and pass on and hand over, will distribute, will cast|διαδίδωμι]] [[nourishment|nourishment and food and victuals, provisions and forage, livelihood and living, a mode of life and life, that which provides sustenance, nurture and rearing and bringing up, education, a brood|τροφή]].

names.gloss: (Βενιαμιν, from Hebrew Binyāmîn, "son of the right hand" or "son of the south")

greek: Πάντες οὗτοι υἱοὶ Ιακωβ δώδεκα, καὶ ταῦτα ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς ὁ πατὴρ αὐτῶν καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτούς, ἕκαστον κατὰ τὴν εὐλογίαν αὐτοῦ εὐλόγησεν αὐτούς.
hint: These are the twelve sons of Jacob, and their father blessed each with his own blessing.

notes.text: Each, according to his blessing, he blessed them: the singular and the plural together, as the Hebrew has ʾîš … bērak ʾōtām.

reading: [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] sons of [[name:Ιακωβ]] twelve, and [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped|λαλέω]] to them [[the father|the father, the grandfather|πατήρ]] of them and [[spoke well of|spoke well of, praised, honoured, blessed|εὐλογέω]] them, [[every|every, every one, each, each one, all and each one, singly and by itself, each by himself|ἕκαστος]] [[down|down, downwards, down from, down upon, over, upon|κατά + accusative]] [[the good language|the good language, the fine language, the fair speech and specious talk, the eulogy and panegyric, the blessing|εὐλογία]] of him [[spoke well of|spoke well of, praised, honoured, blessed|εὐλογέω]] them.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐγὼ προστίθεμαι πρὸς τὸν ἐμὸν λαόν· θάψατέ με μετὰ τῶν πατέρων μου ἐν τῷ σπηλαίῳ, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ Εφρων τοῦ Χετταίου,
hint: Jacob, about to be gathered to his people, asks to be buried with his fathers in the cave in Ephron's field.

notes.text: The present of προστίθημι in the passive: I am being added to my people.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to them I [[I am put to|I am put to, I am handed over and delivered, I am given and bestowed, I am imposed further, I am attributed, I am added|προστίθημι]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the mine|the mine, the to me and relating to me and against me, the by me|ἐμός]] [[people|people, men, soldiers, land-army, common men, folk, Jews, Christians|λαός]]; [[pay the last dues to a corpse|pay the last dues to a corpse and honour with funeral rites, bury and inter|θάπτω]] me [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of|μετά + genitive]] [[of the fathers|of the fathers, of the grandfathers|πατήρ]] of me [[in the grotto|within, inside of, and by means of the grotto and cave and cavern|ἐν; σπήλαιον]], which is [[in the field|within, inside of, and by means of the field, the lands, the farm, the country|ἐν; ἀγρός]] of [[name:Εφρων]] of the [[name:Χετταίου]],

names.gloss: (Εφρων, from Hebrew ʿEprôn, of uncertain meaning)
(Χετταῖος, the man of Χετ, Heth; Hebrew Ḥittî)

greek: ἐν τῷ σπηλαίῳ τῷ διπλῷ τῷ ἀπέναντι Μαμβρη ἐν τῇ γῇ Χανααν, ὃ ἐκτήσατο Αβρααμ τὸ σπήλαιον παρὰ Εφρων τοῦ Χετταίου ἐν κτήσει μνημείου·
hint: The double cave facing Mamre in Canaan, which Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite as a burial holding.

notes.text: As a possession of a tomb, for the Hebrew laʾăḥuzzat-qāber, a burial holding, as at 23:20.

reading: [[in the grotto|within, inside of, and by means of the grotto and cave and cavern|ἐν; σπήλαιον]] [[to the twofold|to the twofold and double, to the double-minded and treacherous|διπλοῦς]] to the thing [[opposite|opposite and against|ἀπέναντι]] of [[name:Μαμβρη]] [[in the earth|within, inside of, and by means of the earth, the land, the ground|ἐν; γῆ]] of [[name:Χανααν]], which [[procured for himself|procured for himself, got, gained, acquired, brought upon himself and incurred, procured for another|κτάομαι]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[the grotto|the grotto and cave and cavern|σπήλαιον]] [[from the side of|from the side of, from beside, from, near|παρά + genitive]] of [[name:Εφρων]] of the [[name:Χετταίου]] [[in acquisition|within, inside of, and by means of acquisition, possession, possessions and property|ἐν; κτῆσις]] [[of memorial|of memorial, of remembrance, of record, of monument|μνημεῖον]];

names.gloss: (Μαμβρη, from Hebrew Mamrēʾ, of uncertain meaning)
(Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)
(Αβρααμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrāhām, which the Hebrew of 17:5 hears in ʾab hămôn gôyim, "father of a multitude of nations")

greek: ἐκεῖ ἔθαψαν Αβρααμ καὶ Σαρραν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, ἐκεῖ ἔθαψαν Ισαακ καὶ Ρεβεκκαν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκεῖ ἔθαψα Λειαν
hint: There Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah were buried, and there Jacob buried Leah.

notes.text: They buried, then I buried: Jacob's own act last.

reading: [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] [[paid the last dues to a corpse|paid the last dues to a corpse and honoured with funeral rites, buried and interred|θάπτω]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] and [[name:Σαρραν]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse, the mortal woman|γυνή]] of him, [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] [[paid the last dues to a corpse|paid the last dues to a corpse and honoured with funeral rites, buried and interred|θάπτω]] [[name:Ισαακ]] and [[name:Ρεβεκκαν]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse, the mortal woman|γυνή]] of him, and [[there|there, in that place|ἐκεῖ]] [[I paid the last dues to a corpse|I paid the last dues to a corpse and honoured with funeral rites, I buried and interred|θάπτω]] [[name:Λειαν]]

names.gloss: (Σαρρα, from Hebrew Śārâ, "princess")
(Ισαακ, from Hebrew Yiṣḥāq, "he laughs")
(Ρεβεκκα, from Hebrew Ribqâ, of uncertain meaning)
(Λεια, from Hebrew Lēʾâ, of uncertain meaning, perhaps "wild cow")

greek: ἐν κτήσει τοῦ ἀγροῦ καὶ τοῦ σπηλαίου τοῦ ὄντος ἐν αὐτῷ παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Χετ.
hint: The field and its cave were bought from the sons of Heth.

notes.text: As a possession: the Greek joins this to 49:31. The Hebrew has miqnēh haśśādeh, the purchase of the field, as a statement of its own.

reading: [[in acquisition|within, inside of, and by means of acquisition, possession, possessions and property|ἐν; κτῆσις]] [[of the field|of the field, of the lands, of the farm, of the country|ἀγρός]] and [[of the grotto|of the grotto and cave and cavern|σπήλαιον]] [[of the thing being|of the thing being, of the thing existing|εἰμί]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to it [[from the side of|from the side of, from beside, from, near|παρά + genitive]] of the sons of [[name:Χετ]].

names.gloss: (Χετ, from Hebrew Ḥēt, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ κατέπαυσεν Ιακωβ ἐπιτάσσων τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξάρας τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὴν κλίνην ἐξέλιπεν καὶ προσετέθη πρὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.
hint: Jacob finishes charging his sons, draws his feet up onto the bed, breathes his last and is gathered to his people.

notes.text: καταπαύω, to lay to rest, to make an end: he finished charging his sons.
ἐκλείπω, to leave out, then to fail: he failed. The Hebrew has wayyigwaʿ, he expired.
Having lifted his feet. The Hebrew has wayyeʾĕsōp̄ raglāyw, he gathered up his feet.

reading: and [[laid to rest|laid to rest, put an end to, made to cease, stopped and kept in check, put down|καταπαύω]] [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[putting upon as a duty|putting upon as a duty and enjoining, ordering, imposing commands, placing next or beside, placing behind, placing in reserve, setting in command over|ἐπιτάσσω]] to the sons of him and [[having lifted up|having lifted up and lifted off the earth, having raised in dignity and exalted, having raised and aroused and stirred up, having carried off for himself and earned and won and gained, having taken on himself|ἐξαίρω]] [[the feet|the feet, the talons, the feet of a hill|πούς]] of him [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[the that on which one lies|the that on which one lies and couch, the bed, the bier|κλίνη]] [[left out|left out and omitted and passed over, forsook and deserted and abandoned, suffered an eclipse, died, left off and ceased and stopped, failed and was wanting|ἐκλείπω]] and [[was put to|was put to, was handed over and delivered, was given and bestowed, was imposed further, was attributed, was added|προστίθημι]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward|πρός + accusative]] [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]] of him.
